additional_requirements: manic_episode is present for the majority of the total duration of the active and residual portions of the illness
delusions_and_hallucinations occur for 2 or more weeks in the absence of a major mood episode

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.

subtypes.Diminished Emotional Expression: A state of reduced emotional expression in facial expressions, eye contact, intonation of speech, and movements.
subtypes.Avolition: A decrease in motivated self-initiated purposeful activities.
subtypes.Alogia: A state where the quantity of spontaneous speech is significantly reduced.
subtypes.Anhedonia: A decrease in the ability to experience pleasure or interest in enjoyable activities.
subtypes.Asociality: A state where interest in social activities or interpersonal relationships is significantly reduced.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).

subtypes.Inflated Self-Confidence: Feeling capable of anything and believing that failure is impossible, unlike one's usual self.
subtypes.Overestimation of Abilities: Unrealistically assessing one's talents, knowledge, or abilities as superior.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one is a special and important person with a special mission or purpose.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).

subtypes.Reduced Sleep Duration: Sleeping significantly less than usual but feeling refreshed rather than tired.
subtypes.Loss of Sleep Need: Not feeling the urge to sleep or the thought that sleep is necessary.
subtypes.Indifference to Insomnia: Feeling no problem and continuing activities despite staying up for several nights.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.

subtypes.Talkativeness: Speaking far more than usual and continuing to talk without rest.
subtypes.Rapid Speech: Speech speed is so fast that it is difficult for others to understand or interrupt.
subtypes.Pressured Speech: Cannot stop talking or tolerate silence due to an internal pressure to keep speaking.

symptom.disease_info: Schizoaffective Disorder, Bipolar Type is defined by a longitudinal course in which a person has mood episodes with manic features alongside psychotic symptoms, with delusions or hallucinations also occurring for a period outside the mood episode. It is typically distinguished from bipolar disorder with psychotic features by the persistence of psychosis beyond mood episodes, and from schizophrenia by the prominent, syndromic manic component across the illness course.

patient.stressor: When Scott’s Los Angeles streetwear employer abruptly reorganized around a high-stakes exclusive sneaker launch and gave junior buyers more responsibility, he initially seemed energized by the chance to prove he could read culture faster than anyone else. Over the next 1 year and 3 months, his high-energy work style shifted into sustained elevated and irritable periods, reduced sleep, pressured deal-making, and grandiose certainty about his role in shaping the market, while fixed beliefs and vivid perceptual experiences continued even during stretches when his mood was less charged. As the course progressed, he also became less socially engaged at gallery events and beach-volleyball weekends, and his performance declined through missed deadlines, strained vendor relationships, and impulsive purchasing decisions. He came to psychiatric care after a failed buying trip and a warning from his supervisor led him to use his company’s employee assistance referral, partly because journaling, yoga, and spontaneous travel no longer restored his usual functioning.

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: What really made me come in is that I can't shake the feeling that people at work and even some vendors are tracking my buys and messing with the launch numbers to make me look stupid, even when my supervisor shows me the reports don't prove that.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.
S020.manifestation: Sometimes when I'm in the stockroom or driving back from a vendor meeting, I hear a man's voice like it's coming from right behind me saying, 'Move faster, Scott,' or laughing at my picks, and when I turn around nobody's there.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.
S023.manifestation: On my off days I mostly sit in my apartment scrolling through sneaker drops without really caring, and I dodge texts from friends about volleyball or gallery nights because it feels like too much work to answer.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.
S033.manifestation: I get these stretches where I feel like the whole city is opening up for me and then, if someone questions a purchase order or tells me to slow down, I snap way harder than I mean to.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.
S034.manifestation: When I'm keyed up I can't just handle one task, so I'll be emailing three vendors, making a buy plan, reorganizing samples, and pacing the office like stopping would make me lose the thread.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).
S035.manifestation: I start believing I can spot the next trend before anyone in L.A. and that the whole sneaker market is basically waiting on my decisions, even though I'm still one of the junior buyers.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).
S036.manifestation: There have been plenty of weeks where I sleep maybe three or four hours, wake up feeling wired and ready, and think lying in bed is just wasting time I could use to make moves.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.
S037.manifestation: People tell me I talk over them in meetings because once I start explaining a drop or a deal, the words come so fast I barely notice anyone trying to jump in.

add_requirements.psychotic_symptoms and manic_episode occ: During the weeks when I was barely sleeping, talking nonstop about sneaker trends, and feeling untouchable at work, I was also convinced vendors were manipulating the numbers and sometimes heard that voice pushing me to move faster.
add_requirements.manic_episode is present for the majorit: Looking back, most of the time since this all started has been taken up by those wired or irritable stretches where I was overworking, overconfident, and hard to slow down, with only shorter calmer periods in between.
add_requirements.delusions_and_hallucinations occur for 2: Even during a calmer stretch when I was sleeping more normally and not feeling like I was running the whole market, I still spent a few weeks believing people were tracking my buys and hearing the voice in the stockroom.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: My job has taken a real hit: I missed buying deadlines, damaged vendor relationships, and made impulsive purchasing calls that got me formally warned by my supervisor. I’ve also pulled away from friends and stopped showing up for the gallery nights and volleyball weekends I used to enjoy.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about a year and three months, starting after the company reorganized around that exclusive sneaker launch.
add_requirements.psychotic_symptoms_duration: The suspicious beliefs and the voice have been happening for roughly ten months now.
add_requirements.manic_episode_duration: The elevated, irritable, high-energy stretches have been part of my life for about eleven months.
